title: Five actual graph workflows: architecture baseline

methods.hosting: The real Storybook components are compiled from the pinned source into an isolated local browser bundle; Storybook manager chrome is not included. ETL args and frozen Nirvana data are explicit and identical across diagnostic variants.
methods.scope: Read-only baseline research, no production optimization and no alternative renderer in this matrix. All browser processes serialized using the shared Chromium lock; other agents held heavy CPU work.
methods.sampleCounts: 12 settled operations for low-cost edits and real pointer moves, 4 mounted graph replacements for each replacement kind, 90 measured frames for each camera mode. Two edit warmups, one replacement warmup, and a complete matching 90-frame camera warmup precede measurements.
methods.editObservation: Input timestamp is immediately before the actual public operation. First rAF callback and first backend draw completion are separate observations. Each operation observes at least120ms then two further rAF callbacks; detailed scenes may continue animating. Gross phase totals include every draw in that observation window. firstDrawMs is only the first backend frame.
methods.replacement: graph.setEntities exists; graph.api.setEntities does not. Clone replacement supplies a fresh structured clone with identical IDs and values to an already mounted, warmed graph. Layout replacement changes every block position nonrigidly while preserving IDs and connections, then restores the original positions. Payload cloning/preparation is outside the input timer and reported separately. This is not a cold mount or a new-ID replacement.
methods.patch: The initial JavaScript runtime probe calls graph.updateEntities with partial rows for ten existing blocks and one existing edge, then reverses the patch. This works at runtime but does not satisfy the method TypeScript signature requiring complete TBlock/TConnection rows. Treat the initial12-sample case as a diagnostic only; the type-correct follow-up is authoritative. It is not a benchmark of a particular undo manager.
methods.status: Only real ETL semantics are tested: public statusTag paused↔succeeded (same empty effect-part set, tint/stripe paint), running↔failed (pre-encoded effect-part visibility), real EtlSimulation.act (tag plus touching flow status), explicit running↔idle flow status, and real simulation.setFocus (global dimming). Stock plain Nirvana has no ETL status/focus workflow and no artificial one was added.
methods.selection: Public api.selectBlocks selects ten nearby blocks and api.selectConnections selects one connected edge, then deselects them. The helper calls these two methods sequentially: its external window.signalBatch resolves a second signals-core copy and does not combine graph-internal notifications. Each public method still uses its own library batching. Do not describe this as one atomic graph batch.
methods.pointer: Actual Playwright page.mouse moves in/out of the chosen visible block at scale0.8. Input time is captured by the browser document mousemove capture listener; real graph/HTML interaction handlers run. All twelve hoveredTag values alternate true/false in both fixtures.
methods.camera: Circular pan at overview and0.8, and one smooth logarithmic .01→.95→.01 zoom cycle. RAF interval on row i includes work following the prior callback; row index is not claimed to identify presentation of the current pose.
methods.deadlines: Continuous rAF timestamp gaps are recorded for edits and native camera rAF intervals for motion. A miss is conservatively >17.0ms to avoid classifying rounded16.7ms as a miss of the60Hz budget; display refresh is approximately120Hz. p95/p99 are sorted[floor(p*n)] capped at n-1. With n<10 only individual values/min/max/arithmetic median are reported.
methods.presentation: rAF callbacks and backend completion are not physical presentation/input-to-photon evidence. Browser frame intervals include other same-thread work; replacement intervals can include the separately reported payload preparation before input timestamp.
methods.gpu: Sparse EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 measurements, disjoint results discarded. Not every operation has a GPU sample.
methods.uploads: Canonical path-record source bytes are counted separately from combined upload bytes. Synchronous CPU time/count inside gl.texSubImage2D, bufferSubData, texImage2D and bufferData is aggregated; it does not measure GPU execution or browser driver work after return. No per-record or per-range clock instrumentation.
methods.quality: This baseline matrix checks real mutation/state/count/context invariants. No new image comparison was performed; previous revision pixel checks are not relabelled as evidence for these workflows.
methods.live: Automatic Live timer is off for controlled operations, but stageaction calls the exact simulation mutation method and focus method used by the ETL story. It does not click the HTML action button or include its ancillary React setCounts update. MiniMap is off and mounted layer count0 is asserted. One attached WebGL context is asserted.

limitations: Small counts identify applicability and dominant cost, not a statistically robust optimization acceptance or cross-device performance promise.

A helper-level duplicate signals-core dependency was found after acquisition. This affects the external selection wrapper and preliminary direct-patch comparison, not the real graph.updateEntities/setEntities internal batches, tag operations, camera or pointer handlers. See corrected follow-up diagnostics.
No CPU/GC trace is included in the headline matrix; stalls are not attributed to GC without a separate diagnostic.
Status, selection and hot replacement mutate overlapping library systems; gross timers are inclusive and must not be added together.
The detailed observation window includes ongoing animation. Use firstDrawMs and input latency for single-update costs rather than equating the sum of all draw CPU with one frame.
MiniMap work is intentionally absent by current user preference.
Local temporary paths identify source evidence, not portable dependencies; repeat by freezing identical fixtures for both measurements and applying the documented public operations.

typedSameInternalBatchPatch.method: Final directional causal control, n8 for each method/fixture. A passes complete actual TBlock/TConnection rows to real graph.updateEntities. B supplies the same effective patch and invokes that same real graph.updateEntities closure/internal signals batch, temporarily replacing only existing-ID list updater bodies with per-ID api.updateBlock/api.updateConnection loops. No production source is changed. Public batch semantics, edits and canonical bytes are matched. This only establishes behavior for known-existing IDs; it is not a proposed universal implementation or tested public workaround.
typedSameInternalBatchPatch.ordering: Unbalanced A then B, directional attribution only; not a final optimized-code benchmark.
typedSameInternalBatchPatch.supersedes: Preliminary partial-row and external-window.signalBatch direct probes are retained only as historical diagnostics; their values are not used for the final type-correct API comparison.

lumaSteadyReplay.method: One warmed fixed-time actual frame is recorded as raw WebGL calls and replayed directly using its existing GPU state/resources. CPU submission overhead is isolated from scene preparation. Main framebuffer is byte-compared. This is not an equivalent renderer implementation and excludes hot uploads, context lifecycle, allocation and feature/DX contracts. Timer resolution limits values near0.1ms.
lumaSteadyReplay.poseScope: The graph uses its fit SCALE or0.35 but is recentered on an actual middle block. It is not necessarily the complete graph fit pose and is not the same camera origin as the five-workflow matrix. Full camera frames are included.

pathHeadroom.method: Read-only candidate counts at the recorded camera, comparing current coarse submission with active primitive-owner and per-piece conservative bounds. Counts do not establish a correctness-certified replacement culler or a speedup; counting CPU is instrumentation, not production culling CPU.
pathHeadroom.poseScope: Fit SCALE recentered on an actual middle block, plus0.35. Not necessarily full graph fit or the main matrix pose.

partialPatchCpuProfile.scope: Separate6-operation ETL attribution run using the initial partial-JavaScript-row path. Profile/tracing overhead means its timings are not headline values. GC events span the profiled run including preparation/drain, not proven individual-input stalls.
